text.p: Europe's largest forest group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Thursday it expected its 1997 earnings to be about the same level as 1996, when it made profit before extras and tax of 3.55 billion markka and operating profit of 5.6 billion.
"UPM-Kymmene expects earnings for 1997 to be around the same as in 1996," the company said in a statement with its first-quarter results.

"Sales prices for printing and writing papers are expected to rise, although only marginally during the first half of the year," the company said, citing strong economic growth in Europe as underpinning an increase in general paper consumption.
But in fine paper, it said European production capacity threatened to rise faster than demand during the second half of 1997.
"Market pulp prices probably bottomed out in April," UPM-Kymmene said.
Overall paper stocks held by customers and distributors were "estimated to be about normal", the company said.
Demand for most of its packaging materials and special products was expected to remain strong, and UPM-Kymmene said good demand for sawn timber and plywood was likely to continue.

Engineering group Rauma, in which UPM's holding will fall to around 35 percent after an offering by UPM, had increased its orderbooks and received more new orders in Q1 1997 than in the year-ago period, UPM said.
